To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth response to drought is a time-dependent process and that GWA mapping of time series data is an efficient method to detect QTLs associated with this trait.

(1) plant size under drought conditions was negatively correlated with RWC and (2) GWA mapping of temporal plant growth data identified several QTLs that would not have been detected by GWA mapping of plant size at a single time-point.

(i) plant size was negatively related to relative water content (independent of absolute water content), (ii) plant size in control and drought stress was best described by an exponential growth model, and (iii) GWA mapping of temporal plant growth data identified six time-dependent QTLs for drought tolerance, which were associated with genes involved in water transport, hormone signalling, and transcriptional regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic variation for growth responses to moderate and temporary drought stress in Arabiopsis and with the identification of candidate genes underlying these QTLs.
the genetic control of time-dependent growth in response to moderate drought stress and with the identification of candidate genes for these growth responses.
the identification of genes and pathways that are involved in the response of Arabidopsis to moderate drought stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the identified QTLs are associated with plant size and drought tolerance, and that the most likely candidates are the genes with the strongest expression changes under drought.
the observed QTLs are associated with the drought response, but that the underlying molecular mechanism is not known yet.
the drought tolerance of the Arabidopsis accessions is a result of a complex interplay between flowering time and plant size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic variation in drought tolerance is complex, but can be dissected by a combination of GWA mapping and gene expression studies.
the genetic basis of drought response in Arabidopsis is highly complex, and that the genetic architecture is best revealed by a time-dependent analysis of growth.
the temporal dynamics of growth under drought stress is a promising trait for GWA mapping and that the identified QTLs may be of interest in breeding for drought tolerance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal dynamics of plant size under drought is a powerful trait for GWA studies, which can be used to identify candidate genes for drought tolerance.
time-dependent growth data can be used to identify candidate genes that are involved in drought tolerance and that the use of time-series data in GWA studies can increase the power of QTL detection.
GWA mapping of temporal plant growth data is a powerful approach to identify QTLs that can be linked to underlying candidate genes.
